claim: Parasite resistance has emerged to all current antimalarial drug classes, including the frontline artemisinin therapies.
source: Although the global incidence rate of malaria has declined over the last decade, the number of people worldwide suffering and dying from malaria is now increasing and parasite resistance has emerged to all current antimalarial drug classes, including the frontline artemisinin therapies (WHO, 2022; Phillips et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to WHO 2022 and Phillips et al., 2017

claim: Artemisinin-based combination therapies fail to cure infections in up to 50% of patients in some regions of Asia.
source: Alarmingly, artemisinin-based combination therapies fail to cure infections in up to 50% of patients in some regions of Asia (van der Pluijm et al., 2019) and delayed parasite clearance rates following artemisinin-based therapy (synonymous with decreased parasite susceptibility to artemisinin) has now been detected in Africa (Balikagala et al., 2021), where most malaria deaths occur.
evidence: Supported by citation to van der Pluijm et al., 2019

claim: Delayed parasite clearance rates following artemisinin-based therapy has now been detected in Africa.
source: Alarmingly, artemisinin-based combination therapies fail to cure infections in up to 50% of patients in some regions of Asia (van der Pluijm et al., 2019) and delayed parasite clearance rates following artemisinin-based therapy (synonymous with decreased parasite susceptibility to artemisinin) has now been detected in Africa (Balikagala et al., 2021), where most malaria deaths occur.
evidence: Supported by citation to Balikagala et al., 2021

claim: Most malaria deaths occur in Africa.
source: Alarmingly, artemisinin-based combination therapies fail to cure infections in up to 50% of patients in some regions of Asia (van der Pluijm et al., 2019) and delayed parasite clearance rates following artemisinin-based therapy (synonymous with decreased parasite susceptibility to artemisinin) has now been detected in Africa (Balikagala et al., 2021), where most malaria deaths occur.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the manuscript

claim: The parasite digests up to 75% of host cell Hb to provide amino acids for protein synthesis.
source: The parasite digests up to 75% of host cell Hb to provide amino acids for protein synthesis and this process additionally serves non-anabolic functions, such as maintaining osmotic stability of the infected red blood cell (Liu et al., 2006; Lew et al., 2003; Krugliak et al., 2002; Loria et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2006; Lew et al., 2003; Krugliak et al., 2002; Loria et al., 1999

claim: Haemoglobin digestion serves non-anabolic functions, such as maintaining osmotic stability of the infected red blood cell.
source: The parasite digests up to 75% of host cell Hb to provide amino acids for protein synthesis and this process additionally serves non-anabolic functions, such as maintaining osmotic stability of the infected red blood cell (Liu et al., 2006; Lew et al., 2003; Krugliak et al., 2002; Loria et al., 1999).
evidence: Supported by citations to Liu et al., 2006; Lew et al., 2003; Krugliak et al., 2002; Loria et al., 1999

claim: P. falciparum M1 alanyl aminopeptidase (PfA-M1) and M17 leucyl aminopeptidase (PfA-M17) are two zinc-dependent metalloaminopeptidases involved in the terminal stage of Hb digestion.
source: P. falciparum M1 alanyl aminopeptidase (PfA-M1) and M17 leucyl aminopeptidase (PfA-M17) are two zinc-dependent metalloaminopeptidases involved in the terminal stage of Hb digestion (Edgar et al., 2022; Dalal and Klemba, 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to Edgar et al., 2022; Dalal and Klemba, 2007

claim: Both PfA-M1 and PfA-M17 are thought to be essential for parasite survival.
source: Both PfA-M1 and PfA-M17 are thought to be essential for parasite survival and are promising targets for antimalarial therapy in vitro and in vivo (Edgar et al., 2022; Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Skinner Adams et al., 2007; Skinner Adams et al., 2012; Harbut et al., 2011; McGowan, 2013; Nankya-Kitaka et al., 1998; Bounaadja et al., 2017; Deprez-Poulain et al., 2012; Drinkwater et al., 2016b; Vinh et al., 2019; González-Bacerio et al., 2014; Mistry et al., 2014; Ruggeri et al., 2015; Kannan Sivaraman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: PfA-M1 and PfA-M17 are promising targets for antimalarial therapy in vitro and in vivo.
source: Both PfA-M1 and PfA-M17 are thought to be essential for parasite survival and are promising targets for antimalarial therapy in vitro and in vivo (Edgar et al., 2022; Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Skinner Adams et al., 2007; Skinner Adams et al., 2012; Harbut et al., 2011; McGowan, 2013; Nankya-Kitaka et al., 1998; Bounaadja et al., 2017; Deprez-Poulain et al., 2012; Drinkwater et al., 2016b; Vinh et al., 2019; González-Bacerio et al., 2014; Mistry et al., 2014; Ruggeri et al., 2015; Kannan Sivaraman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Attempts at genetic manipulation of PfA-M1 have been unsuccessful to date.
source: However, attempts at genetic manipulation of PfA-M1 have been unsuccessful to date, which has precluded formal genetic validation of PfA-M1 as a drug target.
evidence: Stated as fact in the manuscript

claim: Bestatin-based inhibitors of PfA-M1 prevent proteolysis of Hb peptides, leading to a swollen digestive vacuole and stalled growth at the trophozoite stage.
source: Bestatin-based inhibitors of PfA-M1 were previously shown to prevent proteolysis of Hb peptides, leading to a swollen digestive vacuole and stalled growth at the trophozoite stage (Harbut et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harbut et al., 2011

claim: Loss of PfA-M17 function through chemical inhibition or conditional knockdown results in stalled growth at the trophozoite stage but does not induce digestive vacuole swelling.
source: Loss of PfA-M17 function through chemical inhibition or conditional knockdown also results in stalled growth at the trophozoite stage but does not induce digestive vacuole swelling (Edgar et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Edgar et al., 2022

claim: Specific loss of PfA-M17 function results in the presence of multiple membrane-bound digestive vacuoles per parasite.
source: Instead, specific loss of PfA-M17 function results in the presence of multiple membrane-bound digestive vacuoles per parasite.
evidence: Stated as a finding in the manuscript

claim: The authors have previously used rational drug design to optimise dual M1 and M17 inhibitors with nanomolar potency across multiple Plasmodium species.
source: We have previously used rational drug design to optimise dual M1 and M17 inhibitors with nanomolar potency across multiple Plasmodium species (Drinkwater et al., 2016b; Vinh et al., 2019; Mistry et al., 2014; Kannan Sivaraman et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous work by the authors

claim: The authors previously reported a selective PfA-M17 inhibitor with potent antimalarial activity.
source: More recently, we reported a selective PfA-M17 inhibitor with potent antimalarial activity (Edgar et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citation to Edgar et al., 2022

claim: The PfA-M1 enzyme is a monomeric protein consisting of four domains.
source: The PfA-M1 enzyme is a monomeric protein consisting of four domains and is widely believed to function in the cytosol, although localisation to other compartments has been reported (Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Harbut et al., 2011; Allary et al., 2002; Azimzadeh et al., 2010; Mathew et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: PfA-M1 is widely believed to function in the cytosol.
source: The PfA-M1 enzyme is a monomeric protein consisting of four domains and is widely believed to function in the cytosol, although localisation to other compartments has been reported (Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Harbut et al., 2011; Allary et al., 2002; Azimzadeh et al., 2010; Mathew et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: PfA-M1 has a broad substrate specificity that includes most basic and hydrophobic amino acids, but preferentially cleaves leucine and methionine.
source: It has a broad substrate specificity that includes most basic and hydrophobic amino acids, but preferentially cleaves leucine and methionine (Allary et al., 2002; Poreba et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Allary et al., 2002; Poreba et al., 2012

claim: PfA-M1 uses a zinc-dependent mechanism to catalyse the release of single amino acids from the N-terminus of short peptides.
source: PfA-M1 uses a zinc-dependent mechanism to catalyse the release of single amino acids from the N-terminus of short peptides.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: All reported inhibitors of PfA-M1 target the enzyme active site and act to chelate the catalytic zinc ion.
source: All reported inhibitors of PfA-M1 target the enzyme active site and act to chelate the catalytic zinc ion (Skinner Adams et al., 2007; Harbut et al., 2011; Deprez-Poulain et al., 2012; Drinkwater et al., 2016b; Vinh et al., 2019; Poreba et al., 2012; McGowan et al., 2009; Flipo et al., 2007; Harbut et al., 2008; Velmourougane et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Obtaining selectivity for PfA-M1 over PfA-M17 is challenging as the enzymes share similar architecture within the active sites and a catalytic mechanism involving zinc ions.
source: Obtaining selectivity for PfA-M1 over PfA-M17 is challenging as the enzymes share similar architecture within the active sites and a catalytic mechanism involving zinc ions (McGowan et al., 2009; McGowan et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to McGowan et al., 2009; McGowan et al., 2010

claim: Very few compounds that selectively inhibit PfA-M1 over PfA-M17 have been reported.
source: As such, very few compounds that selectively inhibit PfA-M1 over PfA-M17 have been reported (Harbut et al., 2011; Bounaadja et al., 2017; Flipo et al., 2007) and unbiased identification of the target in parasites is critical to confirm specificity.
evidence: Supported by citations to Harbut et al., 2011; Bounaadja et al., 2017; Flipo et al., 2007

claim: IVIEWGA can point to genes encoding general drug resistance mechanisms rather than the cellular target.
source: However, IVIEWGA can also point to genes encoding general drug resistance mechanisms rather than the cellular target, and a major goal of new drug development for malaria is the identification of compounds that fail to yield resistant parasites in vitro (irresistible compounds), as these compounds are less likely to result in clinical resistance (Yang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yang et al., 2021

claim: Thermal proteome profiling was recently applied in P. falciparum to successfully identify the targets of several antimalarial compounds.
source: Thermal proteome profiling was recently applied in P. falciparum to successfully identify the targets of several antimalarial compounds (Dziekan et al., 2019; Wirjanata et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dziekan et al., 2019; Wirjanata et al., 2021

claim: Limited proteolysis proteomics has not previously been reported to identify drug targets in P. falciparum.
source: Whereas limited proteolysis proteomics has not previously been reported to identify drug targets in P. falciparum, this approach has successfully mapped protein-small molecule interactions in other complex eukaryotic proteomes (Piazza et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Piazza et al., 2020

claim: MIPS2673 has a significantly lower cLogP (1.45 vs 2.23 for compound 1).
source: This modification resulted in MIPS2673 (compound 4), which has a significantly lower cLogP (1.45 vs 2.23 for 1) and favourable solubility (i.e. the kinetic solubility of MIPS2673 was estimated to be in the 50–100 μg/mL range using nephelometry vs 12.5–25 µg/mL for 1).
evidence: Experimental data from the study

claim: The kinetic solubility of MIPS2673 was estimated to be in the 50–100 μg/mL range using nephelometry.
source: This modification resulted in MIPS2673 (compound 4), which has a significantly lower cLogP (1.45 vs 2.23 for 1) and favourable solubility (i.e. the kinetic solubility of MIPS2673 was estimated to be in the 50–100 μg/mL range using nephelometry vs 12.5–25 µg/mL for 1).
evidence: Experimental data from the study

source: The binding affinities (Ki) of MIPS2673 towards purified, recombinant PfA-M1 show the compound to be a potent inhibitor (Ki = 211 ± 11 nM), with >4-fold selectivity over PfA-M17 (Ki = 921 ± 69 nM).

claim: MIPS2673 has >4-fold selectivity for PfA-M1 over PfA-M17.
source: The binding affinities (Ki) of MIPS2673 towards purified, recombinant PfA-M1 show the compound to be a potent inhibitor (Ki = 211 ± 11 nM), with >4-fold selectivity over PfA-M17 (Ki = 921 ± 69 nM).
evidence: Experimental data from enzyme assays shown in Figure 1B

claim: MIPS2673 inhibits PfA-M17 with a Ki of 921 ± 69 nM.
source: The binding affinities (Ki) of MIPS2673 towards purified, recombinant PfA-M1 show the compound to be a potent inhibitor (Ki = 211 ± 11 nM), with >4-fold selectivity over PfA-M17 (Ki = 921 ± 69 nM).
evidence: Experimental data from enzyme assays shown in Figure 1B

claim: MIPS2673 inhibits PvA-M1 with a Ki of 6.4 ± 0.5 nM.
source: MIPS2673 was significantly more potent against PvA-M1 (Ki = 6.4 ± 0.5 nM) with >155-fold selectivity over PvA-M17 (Ki >1000 nM).

claim: MIPS2673 has >155-fold selectivity for PvA-M1 over PvA-M17.
source: MIPS2673 was significantly more potent against PvA-M1 (Ki = 6.4 ± 0.5 nM) with >155-fold selectivity over PvA-M17 (Ki >1000 nM).

claim: MIPS2673 is non-inhibitory against the PfA-M18 recombinant metalloaminopeptidase (Ki >500 µM).

claim: MIPS2673 is non-inhibitory against the PfAPP recombinant metalloaminopeptidase (Ki >40 µM).
source: We confirmed that MIPS2673 is non-inhibitory against the PfA-M18 (Ki >500 µM) and PfAPP (Ki >40 µM) recombinant metalloaminopeptidases (data not shown).
evidence: Experimental data from enzyme assays

claim: MIPS2673 showed minimal inhibition of ERAP1 and ERAP2 at concentrations below 500 µM.
source: MIPS2673 showed minimal inhibition of ERAP1 and ERAP2 at concentrations below 500 µM (Table 1), whereas MIPS2673 caused >50% inhibition of LTA4H at concentrations above 10 µM (Table 1).

claim: MIPS2673 caused >50% inhibition of LTA4H at concentrations above 10 µM.
source: MIPS2673 showed minimal inhibition of ERAP1 and ERAP2 at concentrations below 500 µM (Table 1), whereas MIPS2673 caused >50% inhibition of LTA4H at concentrations above 10 µM (Table 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Table 1

claim: No cytotoxicity to HEK293 cells was observed with MIPS2673 up to a concentration of 40 µM.
source: No cytotoxicity to HEK293 cells was observed up to a concentration of 40 µM.

claim: At 120 µM, MIPS2673 inhibited HEK293 cellular proliferation by 89% compared to the untreated control.
source: At 120 µM, MIPS2673 inhibited cellular proliferation by 89% compared to the untreated control (Table 2).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Table 2

claim: MIPS2673 has a 72 hr EC50 of 324 nM (250–470 CI) against the P. falciparum 3D7 strain.
source: We found that MIPS2673 has a 72 hr EC50 of 324 nM (250–470 CI) against the laboratory reference strain, 3D7 (Figure 1C), compared with the expected low nanomolar EC50 achieved with the clinically used artemisinin derivative, artesunate, which was analysed in parallel (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1C

claim: MIPS2673 demonstrated no shift in EC50 when tested against a panel of drug-resistant P. falciparum lines.
source: MIPS2673 demonstrated no shift in EC50 when tested against a panel of drug-resistant P. falciparum lines (Table 3).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Table 3

claim: MIPS2673 is most potent against trophozoite-stage parasites.
source: This confirmed MIPS2673 is most potent against trophozoite-stage parasites (Figure 1D), corresponding to the period of peak PfA-M1 expression (Allary et al., 2002) and activity (Gavigan et al., 2001).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1D and supported by citations

claim: The trophozoite stage corresponds to the period of peak PfA-M1 expression.
source: This confirmed MIPS2673 is most potent against trophozoite-stage parasites (Figure 1D), corresponding to the period of peak PfA-M1 expression (Allary et al., 2002) and activity (Gavigan et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citation to Allary et al., 2002

claim: MIPS2673 caused significant growth retardation when compared to the untreated control and parasite growth stalled at the ring to trophozoite transition (~16–22 hr post invasion).
source: We found that MIPS2673 caused significant growth retardation when compared to the untreated control and parasite growth stalled at the ring to trophozoite transition (~16–22 hr post invasion).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 1E

claim: MIPS2673 has transmission-blocking activity and is most potent against early gametocytes (stages I-III).
source: We found that MIPS2673 has transmission-blocking activity and is most potent against early gametocytes (stages I-III), compared to late (stages IV-V) and mature (stage V) stages (Table 4), but is less potent than the artemisinin derivative, artesunate.
evidence: Experimental data shown in Table 4

claim: Among 1632 proteins reproducibly detected, five proteins were consistently stabilised at both drug concentrations compared to DMSO.
source: Among 1632 proteins reproducibly detected with a minimum of two peptides across two independent experiments (each with at least three independent incubations of MIPS2673 or vehicle with protein lysate), five proteins were consistently stabilised at both drug concentrations compared to DMSO (Figure 3A, Figure 3—source data 1, and Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: Experimental data from thermal stability proteomics shown in Figure 3A

claim: PfA-M1 (PF3D7_1311800) was one of the most significantly stabilised proteins (p<0.01 at 1 µM).
source: Of these, PfA-M1 (PF3D7_1311800) was one of the most significantly stabilised proteins (p<0.01 at 1 µM).
evidence: Experimental data from thermal stability proteomics shown in Figure 3A

claim: PfA-M1 exhibited concentration-dependent stabilisation in the presence of MIPS2673, with an average stabilisation of 1.8-fold and 2.8-fold at 1 µM and 4 µM, respectively.
source: PfA-M1 exhibited concentration-dependent stabilisation in the presence of MIPS2673, with an average stabilisation of 1.8-fold and 2.8-fold at 1 µM and 4 µM, respectively, relative to the untreated control (Figure 3B).
evidence: Experimental data from thermal stability proteomics shown in Figure 3B

claim: The PfA-M17 protein was not stabilised by MIPS2673 at either drug concentration after a 60°C thermal challenge.
source: The PfA-M17 protein was not stabilised by MIPS2673 at either drug concentration after a 60°C thermal challenge (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental data from thermal stability proteomics shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1

claim: The expected target, PfA-M1 aminopeptidase, was the only protein reproducibly identified as the MIPS2673 target across both independent limited proteolysis experiments.
source: The expected target, PfA-M1 aminopeptidase, was the only protein reproducibly identified as the MIPS2673 target across both independent limited proteolysis experiments.
evidence: Experimental data from LiP-MS experiments

claim: The median minimum distance between the significant LiP-MS peptides and bound MIPS2673 was 6.5 Å, significantly less than the 13.2 Å median distance for all detected PfA-M1 peptides (p=0.025).
source: The median minimum distance between the significant LiP-MS peptides and bound MIPS2673 was 6.5 Å, significantly less than the 13.2 Å median distance for all detected PfA-M1 peptides (p=0.025) (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Experimental data from structural analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Among the nine structurally significant LiP-MS peptides, four contained atoms within Van der Waals distance (<4 Å) of MIPS2673.
source: Among the nine structurally significant LiP-MS peptides, four contained atoms within Van der Waals distance (<4 Å) of MIPS2673.
evidence: Experimental data from structural analysis

claim: The minimum distance between the centre of mass of significant LiP peptides and MIPS2673 was 5.2 Å.
source: The minimum distance between this point and MIPS2673 was 5.2 Å and the MIPS2673 centre of mass neighbourhood (residues within 6.44 Å of the centre of mass) overlapped with the binding site (Figure 5C).
evidence: Experimental data from structural analysis shown in Figure 5C

claim: Of the 201 putative peptides identified, 97 were significantly dysregulated (p<0.05) following MIPS2673 treatment.
source: Of the 201 putative peptides identified, 97 were significantly dysregulated (p<0.05).
evidence: Experimental data from metabolomics analysis

claim: The majority of dysregulated peptides were significantly increased (fold-change >1.5 and p<0.05) in abundance in MIPS2673-treated cultures compared to DMSO control, indicative of aminopeptidase inhibition.
source: The majority of dysregulated peptides were significantly increased (fold-change >1.5 and p<0.05) in abundance in MIPS2673-treated cultures compared to DMSO control, indicative of aminopeptidase inhibition.
evidence: Experimental data from metabolomics analysis and inference about mechanism

claim: ~80% of significantly dysregulated peptides could be mapped to one of the Hb chains.
source: Overall, ~80% of significantly dysregulated peptides could be mapped to one of the Hb chains, with nearly all increasing in abundance following treatment with MIPS2673 compared to DMSO control.
evidence: Experimental data from metabolomics analysis

claim: Hb chains α and β were the most highly matched protein compared to the remaining infected red blood cell proteome.
source: By this measure, Hb chains α and β were the most highly matched protein compared to the remaining infected red blood cell proteome (Figure 6C; red bars), indicating that MIPS2673 predominantly, but not exclusively, disrupts Hb digestion.
evidence: Experimental data from metabolomics analysis shown in Figure 6C

claim: MIPS2673 predominantly, but not exclusively, disrupts Hb digestion.
source: By this measure, Hb chains α and β were the most highly matched protein compared to the remaining infected red blood cell proteome (Figure 6C; red bars), indicating that MIPS2673 predominantly, but not exclusively, disrupts Hb digestion.
evidence: Inference from experimental data shown in Figure 6C

claim: A direct comparison of peptide perturbations induced by MIPS2673 and MIPS2571 showed clearly distinct peptide profiles.
source: However, a direct comparison of peptide perturbations induced by MIPS2673 and MIPS2571 (data from Edgar et al., 2022) showed clearly distinct peptide profiles.
evidence: Experimental data comparing metabolomics profiles

claim: A subset of short basic peptides (containing Lys or Arg) were elevated following exposure to MIPS2673, but not the PfA-M17 inhibitor.
source: Whilst many peptides accumulated with both inhibitors, the extent of peptide accumulation differed, and a subset of short basic peptides (containing Lys or Arg) were elevated following exposure to MIPS2673, but not the PfA-M17 inhibitor (Figure 6A).
evidence: Experimental data shown in Figure 6A

claim: The gene encoding PfA-M1 was previously shown to be refractory to knockout and is predicted to be essential for blood-stage growth.
source: The gene encoding PfA-M1 was previously shown to be refractory to knockout and is predicted to be essential for blood-stage growth, making it an attractive antimalarial drug target (Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dalal and Klemba, 2007; Zhang et al., 2018

claim: DIA-based protein quantification results in high run-to-run reproducibility and a comprehensive dataset that is not biased towards highly abundant proteins.
source: DIA-based protein quantification also results in high run-to-run reproducibility and a comprehensive dataset that is not biased towards highly abundant proteins (Siddiqui et al., 2022b; Gillet et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Siddiqui et al., 2022b; Gillet et al., 2012

claim: The DIA-based thermal stability proteomics workflow identified approximately 47% of the detectable P. falciparum blood-stage proteome.
source: Our DIA-based thermal stability proteomics workflow identified approximately 47% of the detectable P. falciparum blood-stage proteome (Siddiqui et al., 2022a), with the undetected proteins primarily comprised of membrane-bound proteins that are not readily extracted with detergent-free buffers required for stability assays of soluble proteins.
evidence: Experimental data from the study with citation to Siddiqui et al., 2022a

claim: MIPS2673 acts by chelating the catalytic zinc ion of the PfA-M1 active site.
source: Our structural analysis showed that MIPS2673 acts by chelating the catalytic zinc ion of the PfA-M1 active site, similar to all other inhibitors produced to date (Skinner Adams et al., 2007; Harbut et al., 2011; Deprez-Poulain et al., 2012; Drinkwater et al., 2016b; Vinh et al., 2019; Poreba et al., 2012; McGowan et al., 2009; Flipo et al., 2007; Harbut et al., 2008; Velmourougane et al., 2011).
evidence: Experimental data from X-ray crystallography and supported by citations

claim: MIPS2673 demonstrated excellent selectivity over several human M1 homologues.
source: A strategy targeting the catalytic zinc may present challenges for achieving selectivity over host zinc-dependent enzymes, but MIPS2673 demonstrated excellent selectivity over several human M1 homologues, providing rationale for further development of M1 selective inhibitors that present a low risk of host toxicity.
evidence: Experimental data from enzyme assays

claim: The structurally significant peptides identified with LiP-MS included the peptide S292EVIIHPETNYALT305, which guards the entrance pathway to the active site.
source: The structurally altered peptides identified with LiP-MS included the peptide S292EVIIHPETNYALT305, which guards the entrance pathway to the active site and is likely involved in substrate recognition and catalytic competence of the enzyme structure (Papakyriakou and Stratikos, 2017) as well as the peptide L449NLVAVSDFNVGAMENK465, which contains the highly conserved GAMEN exopeptidase motif (McGowan et al., 2009).
evidence: Experimental data from LiP-MS and supported by citation to Papakyriakou and Stratikos, 2017

claim: The peptide L449NLVAVSDFNVGAMENK465 contains the highly conserved GAMEN exopeptidase motif.
source: The structurally altered peptides identified with LiP-MS included the peptide S292EVIIHPETNYALT305, which guards the entrance pathway to the active site and is likely involved in substrate recognition and catalytic competence of the enzyme structure (Papakyriakou and Stratikos, 2017) as well as the peptide L449NLVAVSDFNVGAMENK465, which contains the highly conserved GAMEN exopeptidase motif (McGowan et al., 2009).
evidence: Experimental data from LiP-MS and supported by citation to McGowan et al., 2009

claim: The GAMEN motif functions to bring substrate to the active site metal for catalysis and contributes hydrogen bonds for ligand binding.
source: The GAMEN motif functions to bring substrate to the active site metal for catalysis and contributes hydrogen bonds for ligand binding (McGowan et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citation to McGowan et al., 2009

claim: PfA-M1 has been shown to play an essential role in the terminal stages of Hb digestion and the generation of an amino acid pool within the parasite cytosol.
source: PfA-M1 has been shown to play an essential role in the terminal stages of Hb digestion and the generation of an amino acid pool within the parasite cytosol (Harbut et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harbut et al., 2011

claim: Turnover of Hb into oligopeptides and amino acids peaks during the trophozoite stage when PfA-M1 expression and activity is highest.
source: Turnover of Hb into oligopeptides and amino acids peaks during the trophozoite stage when PfA-M1 expression and activity is highest.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge

claim: Inhibition of PfA-M1 using an activity-based probe based on the bestatin scaffold resulted in trophozoite-stage stalling of parasite growth.
source: Inhibition of PfA-M1 using an activity-based probe based on the bestatin scaffold resulted in trophozoite-stage stalling of parasite growth (Harbut et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Harbut et al., 2011

claim: The activity-based probe also caused digestive vacuole swelling, a phenotype that was not observed with MIPS2673.
source: However, the activity-based probe also caused digestive vacuole swelling, a phenotype that we did not observe.
evidence: Comparison of experimental observations

claim: PfA-M1 is a cytoplasmic protein.
source: Since PfA-M1 is a cytoplasmic protein (Mathew et al., 2021), which is presumed to digest short peptides exported from the digestive vacuole, specific inhibition of this enzyme with MIPS2673 is unlikely to cause digestive vacuole swelling.
evidence: Supported by citation to Mathew et al., 2021

claim: Specific inhibition of PfA-M1 with MIPS2673 is unlikely to cause digestive vacuole swelling.
source: Since PfA-M1 is a cytoplasmic protein (Mathew et al., 2021), which is presumed to digest short peptides exported from the digestive vacuole, specific inhibition of this enzyme with MIPS2673 is unlikely to cause digestive vacuole swelling.
evidence: Inference based on known localization and experimental observations

claim: MIPS2673 is non-inhibitory towards recombinant PfA-M18 and PfAPP, even at concentrations >120-fold above the EC50 for in vitro parasite killing.
source: PfA-M18 and PfAPP are unlikely to be true off-targets that contribute to the antimalarial mechanism in parasites as we found MIPS2673 is non-inhibitory towards recombinant versions of these enzymes, even at concentrations >120-fold above the EC50 for in vitro parasite killing.
evidence: Experimental data from enzyme assays

claim: PfA-M17 was not stabilised by MIPS2673 in the thermal stability proteomics dataset at 60°C.
source: However, PfA-M17 was not stabilised by MIPS2673 in our thermal stability proteomics dataset at 60°C, a temperature that we previously showed stabilised PfA-M17 when bound to an inhibitor (Edgar et al., 2022), and specific loss of PfA-M17 function results in multiple membrane-bound digestive vacuoles per parasite, a phenotype not observed in parasites treated with MIPS2673.
evidence: Experimental data from thermal stability proteomics
